intro_html: The "Swiss Tibet": a vast, windswept, tundra-like protected high-altitude plateau offering Alpine solitude and sweeping 360° views across the Lepontine Alps. A timeless Alpine crossing through one of Switzerland's most remote and ecologically precious landscapes.

routes.title_html: Vrin → Greina Plateau (Plaun la Greina) via Voradetsch — Full day route (~5–6 hours, ~900 m elevation gain). Vrin (1453 m) → Voradetsch hut zone (~2100 m, ~2.5–3 h) → Plaun la Greina plateau crest (2355 m, ~1 h further). Return by the same route (~3–4 h down).

getting_there.by_pt_html: Train: Zürich HB → Disentis/Mustér (RhB Gotthard line, ~2.5 h). The famous "Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn" passes through Disentis. PostBus: Disentis/Mustér → Sumvitg → Vrin (line 570 or regional variant; ~45 min—1 h, seasonal/daily variations). Check PostBus timetable and SBB trip planner (combined ticket recommended). Return: Vrin → PostBus to Sumvitg/Disentis → Train back to Zürich or regional hub.
getting_there.by_car_html: Drive to Vrin via Sumvitg (Graubünden). From Chur, take the main road north via Ilanz toward Disentis; turn east into the Sumvitg valley. The road ends at the small village of Vrin (1453 m). Park near the village center or at the trailhead lots. Approximate drive from Zürich: ~2.5 hours.

lapse_rate.example_html: 18 °C at Disentis → ~13.5 °C at plateau (or cooler with wind chill; sustained winds can make -5 °C feel like -15 °C).

weather.season_html: July–September is the reliable window; August typically has the calmest weather and most reliable snow-free conditions. Early June can still have patches of hard snow above 2200 m. October is possible but increasingly risky (early frost, sudden weather swings). Avoid after fresh snow — the plateau becomes treacherous and navigation is difficult.

takeaways_html: Crowding paradox: Despite notoriety, plateau less crowded than nearby routes; 30–60 hikers/day peak August.
Weather volatility: Föhn corridor creates rapid pressure/temperature swings; barometer useful.
Solitude finding: Midweek (June, September) offers exceptional isolation near major pass.

reports.title: Vrin to Greina Plateau — Swiss Tibet
bullets_html: Remote alpine tundra-like terrain with minimal vegetation
Wind dominates plateau experience; can exceed 60 km/h
Navigation minimal on marked trail; hazardous in whiteout

reports.title: Plaun la Greina in perfect alpine weather
bullets_html: Protected alluvial site; stay on marked paths to minimize damage
360° views to Säntis, Glarus peaks, Gotthard region
Early-season snow patches require microspikes before late June

gear.title: Essential
items_html:
• Hiking poles
  • Sun protection (cream + glasses + hat)
  • 2 L water
  • Emergency snacks

safety_html: Rapid deterioration: Cloud ceiling drops to <100m in 15 min; whiteout risk high.
Navigation: Limited markers; cairn-dependent; GPS critical in fog.
Wind gusts >60 km/h: Common afternoon; dangerous on exposed ridge.
Dehydration: Thin air, low humidity; 3+ liters recommended.
Hypothermia: Plateau lacks windbreak; temperature perception error.
Rockfall/scree: Unstable sections; descending hikers dislodge rocks.
Turn back if thunderstorms develop — lightning risk above treeline is extreme.
disclaimer_html: This page is an informal hike plan, not professional mountain-safety advice. Conditions change rapidly. Always check MeteoSwiss and SAC before setting out.
